method.counters: scripts/darwin_process_usage.c compiled with cc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror to runs/darwin-process-usage-20261109. Official SDK RUSAGE_INFO_V6 and libproc APIs, only own benchmark PIDs. Per-request before/after snapshots added through optional --usage-helper. Python scripts/darwin_usage.py preserves raw fields and derives diagnostic ratios; evaluator verifies raw hashes, responses and counter arithmetic.
method.time_units: CPU times are Mach ticks, not nanoseconds. mach_timebase_info returns125/3. Converted CPU time independently calibrated against a controlled child's process_time_ns: ratio1.0000977494135037. Hardware cycles/instructions remain raw counters.
method.scope: OS counter snapshots bracket the HTTP interval but are not exactly coextensive: helper invocation/return and a small amount of server housekeeping can fall inside the counter interval. Helper CPU is charged to a separate process. Neither helper invocation nor metrics scrape is included in HTTP wall time. CPU time is aggregate across server threads, not model-only CPU time.
method.interpretation: P-only accounting is mapped by XNU task_power_info_locked/recount performance-kind accounting. No affinity or clock guarantee. cycles_per_cpu_ns is an aggregate rate proxy, not direct frequency. Do not normalize wall time by this proxy to claim a speedup.
